title: Colton Herta penalised following Baku Qualifying
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of Thursday’s FIA Formula 2 Qualifying in Baku, Colton Herta has been penalised.

Herta has been handed a grid penalty for Feature Race 2 for impeding Cian Shields during Qualifying 2.

After hearing from both drivers, along with their respective team representatives, the Stewards determined that Herta had unnecessarily impeded Shields between at Turn 14, breaching Article 31.6 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.

As a result, they elected to hand Herta a three-place grid penalty for Feature Race 2.

title: Round 12 Post Qualifying 2 Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2: Hello again, this time for the FIA Formula 2 post-Qualifying 2 Press Conference here at Baku City Circuit. Joining us in third place, Rafael Câmara from Invicta Racing. In second place, Alexander Dunne for Rodin Motorsport and, also for Rodin Motorsport, taking his first pole position of 2026, Martinius Stenshorne. Martinius, welcome back to this couch. The roles are reversed in Qualifying 2. You lead the Rodin one-two. Congratulations. Can you tell us about that lap? You were flying.

Martinius Stenshorne: Yeah, the lap was pretty good. Also, I managed to get a good tow. It was perfect. Good strategy from the team as well to box and get one final lap on another set. So, I think we really maximised our session and we improvised well with the strategy. So, really happy.

FIA Formula 2: Were you able to take anything from that first qualifying session and use it in the second, despite the quick turnaround?

Stenshorne: Yeah, well, you find the limits and then it doesn’t change too much. Obviously, we go a bit quicker, there’s a bit more grip and the car is a bit lighter as well. So, we took some learnings from Q1 into Q2 and left it all out there.

FIA Formula 2: You said pre-weekend that you were looking to fight for the top spots and, so far, so good. What are you expecting for the rest of the round in the races?

Stenshorne: Well, I think now we have a good starting point, so that makes life a bit easier, but there’s still a long way to go. Two long races, well, three long races in total this weekend. So there’s still a lot of work to do, but it’s a good beginning.

FIA Formula 2: A very good beginning indeed. Congrats. Alex, thank you for waiting. P2 and another strong qualifying showing for you. You had a distant tow, but was it a little bit too far back to gain pace in that final sector?

Alexander Dunne: Yeah, I think I was probably a little bit too far behind. I think, in general, my lap in Q2 was pretty bad as well. My lap in Q1 was obviously quite good, but in Q2 there were a couple of mistakes. But I think, in general, it’s a difficult track, so to do two perfect laps across both sessions is always going to be difficult. But, no, in the end, to be on the front row is not the end of the world.

FIA Formula 2: It’s a very strong day for the team and exactly the kind of performance you needed with the title race still on. What makes it so special for you out there? We know that you love street circuits, but today you really showed that this is your kind of circuit.

Dunne: Yeah, I think it’s just something I enjoy. I think pushing to the limit, being close to the walls. I think this track is also different, where you’re approaching a lot of heavy braking zones from very high speed, which you don’t necessarily have on a street circuit. So I think it tests you in a lot of different areas, but it’s really enjoyable and it’s really cool. I think I said at the beginning of the weekend that qualifying is always something that a driver enjoys the most, so the fact that we had two goes at it made it a lot of fun as well. I think it was nice that, whatever you had in Q1, you had an opportunity to go out again, push the limits again, and learn and improve on what you did in Q1. So, definitely it’s a lot of fun. I think if we could do it all the time, I’d like to keep this format because it’s really enjoyable. But the track is super cool as well.

FIA Formula 2: Thank you very much. Congratulations on a great day. Moving on to Rafael, P3 in Q2. Are you happy with that result today?

Rafael Câmara: Yeah, I think overall it was a decent qualifying. Obviously, from Q1, I think we had a good base and I was able to feel more comfortable with the car in that second qualifying. Probably, I think, with the strategy we didn’t maximise, but I’m pretty happy with where we’re starting. Here in Baku as well, there’s always plenty of action in the races, so for sure there will be a lot going on on Sunday. So let’s see how it will be.

FIA Formula 2: Speaking of strategy, we saw you were out on track, but then opted to pit rather than try for a final improvement. Was that a strategy call the team made ahead of time or one that was decided during the session?

Câmara: Yeah, I mean, in the end, I think we didn’t really maximise things. For sure, we could have done a better job. I think what we did, in a way, was not really what we needed to be there fighting for position. But, in the end, I think the first lap was good enough that we’re still in a place where we can fight. Like I said, I’m quite happy with what we did and, from there, we can grab some good points.

FIA Formula 2: Like you said, you’re in a great position in both races this weekend, even in the Sprint Race. You must be feeling good about your chances of overturning the points deficit in the title race. You are seven points behind Tsolov at the moment.

Câmara: Yeah, for sure. In qualifying, we were better than him and, for sure, it gives us a better chance already with the starting positions. But we know how he is too, and we know that a lot of things can happen. So, for sure, we need to keep focused, keep our heads down, and the championship is still far from over. I think we just need to keep focusing on ourselves, make sure that we always try to maximise what we can and don’t leave anything on the table because we know how competitive he is. We always need to be there and be consistent to make sure that we can fight for the championship

title: Mari Boya: 'More to come' as he eyes triple score following best qualifying of 2026
excerpt:
Mari Boya was very happy with his and PREMA Racing's efforts in Baku Qualifying, finishing up P6 and P4 in sessions one and two respectively.

The Spaniard was even eying up a better result as he completed his lap in Q2 without a slipstream down the main start/finish straight.

Boya was pleased despite the potential left on the table, explaining that things were smooth from the first lap in Practice for PREMA in Baku.

"I'm feeling super good," he said in the paddock after the sessions. "It's a feeling I would say I forgot about. But I think there's still something in there. I needed this result, it's my first time in Baku and I think the momentum from Madrid is helping, but as I said, we've had a lot of transition in the team.

"For a driver, it's tough because you need to adapt to the category but now we're pushing a lot, and every week we are improving.

"I felt we deserved a top ten in qualifying, maybe two rounds earlier. Even with bad luck, we were fighting here, and I think we proved we can be at the front. Being alone on a track without much slipstream, I feel even better.

Boya says that there is pace to unlock in the car between Thursday and Friday

"And also around a super technical track, and again, it’s new for me. It's something I'm really proud of. There's a lot of work behind the scenes and now it's starting to pay off. I'm the same guy from the beginning of the season, simply with a better environment around me."

PREMA opted to put Boya in clean air for his final run instead of getting involved in the games between multiple drivers for track position.

READ MORE

QUALIFYING: Rodin sweep Baku sessions as Dunne and Stenshorne take poles

Though he lost out on a tow to the line, it meant his lap was down to pure pace, something he says is looking good this weekend.

He added that it left him feeling mixed with the thought of a potential top three on the cards had he gone with the tow. But he praised his team for how they managed a difficult session.

"It was really important to execute the plan you had in mind with your team and just focus on that. There are so many things that can happen during a session, and you just need to do what you want to do the best you can. And I think it's what we did.

The Spaniard is targetting points in all three races this weekend in Baku

"We had a good conversation with the team and radio messages and they made good calls, and I think it was well executed. It was a good call for the second set and even going alone we did the lap time, so I'm happy with it.

"It's also strange asking for a pole or maybe wanting a pole because I've never been in the top 10 this season. But, I'm really optimistic and I think P2 was more than possible. Still, I'm happy and I will take it, it's a good position to start both races."

Looking ahead to the Friday races, Boya is aiming to secure vital points after a tough campaign to date.

He says the team will be diving into the data overnight as he feels there's even more pace to come from his car, something he believes bodes well for the remainder of Round 12.

"There's still things to work on. When you are more within the window in the car, it's even easier to identify where you need the last bits to make progress. When you are lost, it's difficult to identify the main issue and then work.

"I feel there are still a few bits that we can improve, being in the top five and having things to improve feels amazing. Something new for me this year."

title: Round 12 Post Qualifying 1 Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2: Hello and welcome to today’s FIA Formula 2 post-Qualifying 1 Press Conference here at Baku City Circuit. Joining us in third place, Noel León for Campos Racing. In second place, Martinius Stenshorne for Rodin Motorsport, and, for the first time on Pole Position in 2026, Alexander Dunne, also for Rodin Motorsport. Alex, congratulations. Finally, Pole Position in Feature Race 1, you’ve been quick all day. How happy are you right now?

Alexander Dunne: I’m very happy. I think this is probably the first time I’ve properly smiled all year. No, I mean, I’m very, very pleased. I think, obviously, it shows that the team have done a fantastic job with the car as well. The fact that we were one-two in both qualifying sessions, I think, obviously, as drivers, we did a good job, but in terms of team performance, that’s also pretty impressive from the team side as well. So I think credit goes just as much to them as it does to myself. So, I’m very happy. I think to finally have the opportunity to put it all together and put it on pole feels really nice.

FIA Formula 2: Track position was a key factor in the sessions today. How difficult is that to manage from the car?

Dunne: It’s quite tricky. I think, at least on my side, I was always behind someone, but I never really had the perfect slipstream. I think the slipstream I had in Q1 was a lot better than what I had in Q2. But then it’s always difficult to manage because if you’re behind someone who’s maybe a little bit slower than you, then through the lap you might end up closer than what you’d ideally like to be, which compromises sector two, but then you gain it back in sector three. So, it was quite tricky. There was a lot more of a traffic jam, let’s say, than what I expected. I think in Q1, coming out of Turn 6, we were all in a line and, at one point, I thought there was going to be a crash because everyone was going so slow. In Q2, it was the same thing coming out of 15, I think it is, or 16, where a lot of people slowed down. So it was quite difficult to manage. I would say here it was probably more difficult than Monza because here I would say slipstream is even more important than Monza, and Monza is the one that everyone talks about for traffic management and things like that. So, it was surprisingly more difficult than what it was last year. But in the end, a pole and a P2, I can’t really complain, that’s for sure.

FIA Formula 2: You keep your title hopes going with two more points for Pole Position and a chance for a first victory this season. It has eluded you so far. Are you feeling confident about finally ticking that off tomorrow?

Dunne: Yeah, I think it’s a good way to go about the end of the year, or towards the end of the year. I think after Madrid, it was kind of the first weekend where it all came together again, and we made good progress in terms of catching the guys in the championship. The gap is still relatively big, but I think after that weekend I said I’ll make sure I leave nothing out there for the rest of the season and try to close the gap as much as possible. So far, we’ve started in a good way, but we can just do what we can do. What will be, will be. We’ve done a good job in qualifying and hopefully we can continue that in the races, and then we’ll see where we end up.

FIA Formula 2: Moving on to you, Martinius. It’s P2 for you in Q1, it’s a one-two for Rodin Motorsport and, yet again, you look quick around Baku. You seem to really like this place, don’t you?

Martinius Stenshorne: Yeah, so far we’ve been really quick here. Obviously, I did my first race weekend in Formula 2 last year and that went quite well. We were really competitive. So, yeah, today as well, already from Free Practice, I felt quite confident and I think we showed our pace in qualifying.

FIA Formula 2: Do you think Pole Position was on the table in Q1? You had a tow to the finish line, but getting the perfect track position looked very tricky, at least in Q1 for you.

Stenshorne: Yeah, it was tricky. I mean, no one wants to be in front, which is understandable, and I think it was possible. I had a really good tow, but I think I could have done a bit better in the middle sector there. But in Q2 it all came together and we did everything perfectly.

FIA Formula 2: You said earlier that you had your first F2 race last year at this track and it was good, but you didn’t get the results you deserved. Do you feel like this year is your time to shine?

Stenshorne: Yeah, I hope so. Last year we were really competitive. Unfortunately, we had some issues in both races while being in contention for big points. So, yeah, hopefully this year it turns around and we get it.

FIA Formula 2: Thank you very much. Noel, it’s third place for you in Q1. You managed to find an improvement when a lot of other drivers looked to be struggling to extract another lap. How tough was your session?

Noel León: A bit, to be honest. It was a bit tough to manage the traffic. Everybody was trying to look for a slipstream and it’s quite important. So, at the end of the day, I’m happy with my lap. I think my slipstream wasn’t the best for Q1 and I think we missed pole because of that, but I’m very happy with the performance of the car and the team, and it’s a good position for tomorrow.

FIA Formula 2: Obviously, since the summer, you have been in very good form at this stage of the season. Do you feel that way as well, and do you feel like you’re keeping the momentum through Baku again?

León: Yes, I think so. We had a couple of tough weekends in the summer. Things just didn’t come my way, some stuff was not on my side and I just couldn’t get away from that. So I’m happy that, after Budapest, everything is coming nicely and going better every time. We’ll just keep the momentum until the end of the season. So, yeah, very happy with the progress and we’ll keep pushing.

FIA Formula 2: Tomorrow, you’ll be starting from the clean side of the grid. What will it take to add another win to your tally in 2026?

León: Yeah, I mean, these guys are pretty quick. You can see that they qualified one and two in both qualifying sessions. So it’s going to be tough, I think. As I said, I’m very happy with my lap and with the performance of the team because, in the morning, we didn’t look as strong as we are now. So we are making steps. We’ll try to make another one for tomorrow and we’ll see. These guys, they’re fast. I’ll let you know about that.

title: Gabriele Minì disqualified from Baku Practice
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of FIA Formula 2 Practice in Baku, MP Motorsport driver Gabriele Minì has been disqualified.

Car 9 was summoned to the Stewards after the FIA Technical Delegate reported that an insufficient quantity of fuel remained in the car post-session.

The team could not provide the required 0.8Kg fuel sample after Practice, a potential breach of Article 6.3.1 of the 2026 FIA Formula 2 Technical Regulations.

The Stewards heard from an MP Motorsport team representative and ruled that there was no justifiable reason for the infringement and breach of the Technical Regulations.

As a result, Car 9 is disqualified from the results.

title: Herta enjoying ‘technical’ Baku challenge after positive Free Practice
excerpt:
Colton Herta was happy with his pace after finishing fourth fastest in the Baku Free Practice

Colton Herta described his first 45 minutes of driving around the Baku City Circuit as “enjoyable” but now turns his focus to making sure he can have a good result this weekend.

The Hitech driver showed good form in Free Practice, finishing fourth in the timesheets, 0.495s away from pacesetter Kush Maini’s time.

Speaking in the paddock afterwards, Herta was feeling positive about his first few laps in Azerbaijan.

“It's interesting, I think it's quite technical,” said Herta describing the track. “A lot of really big brake zones, which can be difficult on the street circuit with the bumps and whatnot.

“But it's very enjoyable, I liked it. I like all the tracks this year, they've been enjoyable to drive, and they each have their own little niches in what makes them tick.

“This one is no different. It's very enjoyable, it was very dirty, so it'll be interesting to see the evolution going into qualifying.”

Herta was impressed with the layout of the Baku City Circuit

On the performance so far, Herta was speaking after debriefing with the team, and said so far things are looking positive.

“I was happy with the lap that I did,” he continued. “Obviously, I always want more, and there's still quite a bit to find if you want to be quickest.

READ MORE

‘The car is really quick’ – Maini hails strong start in Baku after going fastest in FP

“So that's kind of what we're working on in between Practice and Qualifying here, to try to set ourselves up as best as possible. There’s a lot of points on offer this weekend, but more so I would just like to get a result.”

Looking ahead to Qualifying later today, conditions are expected to be quite different.

Formula 1 will have their Free Practice before the session, which should improve the grip levels, while temperatures are expected to be warmer. In addition to that, the teams are set to run the Supersoft tyres for the first time.

The Hitech driver wants to deliver a good result this weekend

Herta says all these added factors mean he has a few things to look over before hitting the track.

“I mean, I’m trying to understand really kind of what the difference is,” he said. I want to understand what needs to happen from the driving side of things to get the lap time out of the car.

“I don't think it changes too much as far as the technique from practice. But there's obviously a lot more grip to have.

READ MORE

PRACTICE: Maini and ART Grand Prix quickest in opening Baku session

“So preparing for that and understanding where the biggest jumps come throughout the lap is important.”

Speaking further about his hopes of getting a good result, Herta added: "Every weekend you get more comfortable, and I think on these race weekends, there's really no time to learn.

“You have to be on the pace immediately because of the amount of track time. You then have a bit of a break and are able to understand a little bit more going into these last few rounds.”

Next Up

title: ‘The car is really quick’ – Maini hails strong start in Baku after going fastest in FP
excerpt:
Kush Maini was pleased to have finished fastest in the Baku Free Practice

Kush Maini was impressed with his and his ART Grand Prix team’s start to Round 12 in Baku, as he topped the times in Free Practice.

The Indian driver made a fast start to the session by setting the early benchmark, and with each lap he completed, was a constant presence near the top of the leaderboard.

But with his final lap of the 45-minute outing, Maini completed a 1:56.532 to beat Alexander Dunne to the top time by 0.204s.

Speaking after jumping out of the cockpit, Maini said: “It was really strong. I think all session we were really strong.

“It's a good feeling after Madrid obviously. We were P1 in Madrid as well after Practice and didn't end up racing really. So, nice to be back here in the front.

Maini was fastest in this morning's Free Practice

“Like we said, we know the pace is there. It's just about putting everything together now. It's great to start a doubleheader with good pace, but quali is next and practice means nothing really. So, we'll just take the confidence in the quali and try and re-deliver.

“I mean, the car is very good. It always has been. I think generally me as well, I get up to speed quite quick, even from my first day in F2.

READ MORE

PRACTICE: Maini and ART Grand Prix quickest in opening Baku session

PREVIEW: A supersized weekend in Baku for Round 12

“But I think it's a good starting point and it's time to re-do it again and try and find some time. Everyone's going to find time and quali will be interesting.”

Looking ahead to Qualifying, with the temperature expected to be warmer, a step from the Soft to the Supersoft, and with more rubber laid down by Formula 1’s Free Practice 1, Maini expects a different challenge later today.

“I think obviously with the track rubbering in, it was quite dirty in FP and then the tyres and everything, it'll change the balance a bit,” he explained. “Even the temperature will change the balance a bit.

Maini is expecting a different track for Qualifying later today

“But in the end, we're in the right ballpark and it's about tweaking things. I think from the experience from previous years, we can sort of expect what change is going to be made and from a driving point as well, it's going to be a step forward.

“So, let's see. We know what it takes to get forward. That's pretty good.”

On the fight for pole, Maini who already has two Aramco Pole Position Awards this season – from Miami and Budapest – is hopeful to get two more this evening from Qualifying 1 and 2.

“If I do my best, the car is there and we should be there,” he added. “So, that's all I need to focus on. We'll see.”

Next Up

title: Martinius Stenshorne aiming for Baku rebound and return to podium
excerpt:
Rodin Motorsport's Martinius Stenshorne is eager to get back into the points this weekend around the Baku City Circuit.

The Norwegian made his FIA Formula 2 debut around the track a year ago, impressing in Qualifying to earn P7 in his first outing. He was denied points in both races due to various incidents out of his control, but returning to Baku, the Rodin driver has high hopes for this weekend.

"Last year it was mainly about just getting into the rhythm with the new car," he explained. "It was also a new track for me, so there were quite a lot of things to learn.

"Obviously this year I have a bit more experience coming here, both with the car and the track, so I'm looking forward to it.

"The most difficult thing here is the same as any other street track - the walls are so close, so finding the limit and not being over it but also not too far under it as well is tough.

After learning on the fly one year ago, Stenshorne now has a year's worth of F2 experience to rely upon, and he says that his weekend should be much more straightforward than 12 months ago.

Stenshorne is looking to return to the podium after a tricky spell during the middle part of the year

He is also eager for a good run in all three races this weekend after missing out on a scoring result due to a Safety Car that impacted his strategy and hopes of points.

"It will make it easier. I think we still showed really good pace last year, even though it was first for me. It went really well until it didn't. Hopefully we can carry that good speed into this year and have some good qualifying results and hopefully score some good points in all three races.

"We haven't scored as much as we wanted to lately. It was looking good for a while in Madrid, until another Safety Car came out and kind of ruined our strategy, so hopefully we can get some good points over the line this weekend."

READ MORE

What To Watch For: A few key talking points going into Baku

How to watch Round 12 in Baku: TV, Session times and more

He and the rest of the drivers will have an extra chance of points this weekend, with two Qualifying and Feature Races added to the expanded one-off format for Round 12.

The Rodin driver says that while it won't make much of a difference in terms of approach to the weekend, having an extra race is a welcome addition as he looks to return to the podium for the first time since the Spa Sprint Race.

"It's an extra chance to score some points. I think the preparation has been the same as it usually is, not much has changed. We did our usual sim in the factory.

"The goal now is to be on it from the beginning and pick up some good points on Saturday as well. But for sure the main goal now is to be on it from Thursday and score good points in all three races."

title: James Wharton steps up with TRIDENT for the 2027 season
excerpt:
TRIDENT have announced the signing of James Wharton for the 2027 FIA Formula 2 season.

Wharton steps up from Formula 3 after two seasons, achieving two victories and four podiums in total.

Prior to that, the Australian driver won the 2023 Formula 4 UAE Championship and finished as the runner-up in the 2024 Formula Regional European Championship.

Wharton now graduates to Formula 2 with TRIDENT, having previously raced for the Italian team at Lusail in 2025. Speaking at the announcement, he expressed his delight at the opportunity to work with them once again.

“I really can’t put into words what this opportunity for 2027 means to me,” said Wharton. “To be able to return to TRIDENT after racing with them in 2025 is something really special. We worked very well together and they are a very prestigious team that has done a great job over the last few seasons.

“I’m looking forward to joining the team and continuing to work hard with them over the winter, so that we can arrive in 2027 in the best possible shape. A huge thank you to Giacomo and Maurizio for giving me the opportunity to drive their car and be part of their team. I can’t thank TRIDENT enough, and I’m really looking forward to starting this new chapter of my career.”

TRIDENT Team Manager Giacomo Ricci added: “We are very happy to announce that James Wharton will compete in the 2027 FIA Formula 2 Championship with Trident Motorsport. We got to know him at the end of 2025, when he made his debut with us in F2, and since then we have continued to closely monitor his development. James has demonstrated speed, talent, and great determination. The season just ended allowed him to gain further experience, and we are confident that the work we will do together will enable him to take a significant step forward.”

title: What To Watch For: A few key talking points going into Baku
excerpt:
After a week’s break, the paddock is heading to Baku for Round 12 of this incredible 2026 FIA Formula 2 season.

It could be a critical few days in the title fight in what should be an action-packed few days in Azerbaijan, so we have picked out a few storylines to look for this weekend.

A NEW FORMAT

For the keen onlookers in Madrid, you will have noticed a new weekend format in Formula 3 – with two Qualifying sessions, one Sprint Race and two Feature Races.

Well we are going to have the same with Formula 2 in Baku, meaning that there are 67 points on offer this weekend.

It means the drivers will have a busy Thursday, with Free Practice kicking off the action. Later in the day there are two 20-minute back-to-back Qualifying sessions.

There will be an additional Qualifying session and Feature Race in Baku this weekend

Friday is just as jam-packed with a Sprint Race in the morning and the first Feature Race in the afternoon. All of this before they return for the final race on Saturday.

This will be another test for the drivers as well as their teams as it will be a busy few days. But if it goes well, with the number of points on offer, it could be very rewarding weekend.

READ MORE

How to watch Round 12 in Baku: TV, Session times and more

Inthraphuvasak: 'Points the perfect way to repay the team'

TITLE LEAD IS CRITICAL

With so many points available, those drivers in the title fight will be eager to make sure they maximise their results to give themselves the best chance of being champion.

One of the reasons is that after Baku, there is a two-month before the final two rounds in Lusail and Yas Marina.

An interesting fact is that in the previous nine seasons of Formula 2, the driver who leads the Championship with two rounds to go has gone on to win the title.

The fight to be top at the end of the Baku weekend could be tight

Maybe it will be 10th time lucky for the chasing pack this year, but history shows that you want to be ahead at this time of the season.

With 67 points on offer, a bad weekend for any of the contenders, and a strong performance from their rivals could put them on the back foot heading into the final part of the season.

TSOLOV NEEDS A BOUNCE BACK

At one stage this season Nikola Tsolov could not be stopped. He achieved six victories in the first seven rounds but the four race weekends since have not been as smooth.

The Campos Racing driver still leads the Drivers’ Championship but since his double wins at Silverstone, he has just one podium and two DNFs.

But the inherit pace in each of those race weekends has still been quite strong for Tsolov and Campos, so they will not be too worried.

However, as previously said, the driver that wins the title tends to be the leader going into the final two rounds, so history tells us that is key for Tsolov to maintain his place at the top.

But Rafael Câmara is just seven points behind and with Gabriele Minì and Alexander Dunne having closed the gap in Madrid, Tsolov has a fight on his hands for the championship.

Duerksen has the chance to make history in Baku this weekend

DUERKSEN AIMING FOR HISTORY

There are many drivers in this championship aiming to make history of their own but maybe none are currently as close as Joshua Duerksen.

The Invicta Racing driver returns to Baku – the scene of his first F2 victory in 2024 – with desires on having the outright record for the most wins in the championship.

After Duerksen’s Feature Race victory in Monza, he tied Artem Markelov, Nyck de Vries, Richard Verschoor and Felipe Drugovich on eight wins.

READ MORE

GALLERY: All the best shots from F2's debut in Madrid

Gabriele Minì: 'Title not out of reach' after aggressive drive to points in Madrid

A victory at the venue where it all started would be a great way to own that record, and based on his history in Baku, it is very possible.

As well as the win in 2024, Duerksen finished second in the Feature Race last season – after starting in P14.

So look out for the Paraguayan this weekend, who has already said he wants that record for himself.

title: How to watch Round 12 in Baku: TV, Session times and more
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2 heads back to the streets of Baku for Round 12 of the 2026 campaign, and there's an extra few sessions to keep up with this weekend.

Two Qualifyings will set the grid in Azerbaijan, with an extra Feature Race in the mix in what will be a blockbuster round.

Here's the information you need to keep up with all the goings on.

SESSION TIMES

PRACTICE

Thursday's Practice opens the weekend's offerings with the green light scheduled for 10:00 local time.

QUALIFYING

There will be two Qualifying sessions back-to-back on Thursday. The first begins at 14:00 local time and will last 20 minutes. This session will determine the grid for the Sprint and Feature Race 1.

The second session gets going at 14:30 local time, lasting 20 minutes once again and will set the grid for the second Feature Race on Sunday.

title: Inthraphuvasak: 'Points the perfect way to repay the team'
excerpt:
Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak rebounded from a tough start to the Madrid weekend to earn points on Sunday

It was a weekend of mixed fortunes for Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak, but an impressive comeback drive on Sunday meant he left Madrid with points.

The ART Grand Prix driver suffered a sizeable crash during the opening Practice session of the round, leaving him sidelined for Qualifying and going from the back of the grid.

Using the Safety Car timing to his advantage, the Thai driver was able to launch his way back into the points with sixth position.

Reflecting on the weekend overall, Inthraphuvasak said it was nice to have luck on his side and to reward his team for their hard work.

"After Friday, I never expected to be in this position," Inthraphuvasak admitted. "But I knew that on Sunday, anything could happen - it's Formula 2.

"We saved a set of Softs because we didn't do Qualifying. So I had an extra set of Softs today and we went for the gamble on the strategy and it paid off. So it feels good to turn things around. Obviously, luck was on our side today, but it's a bit of luck I think we were owed.

The Thai driver was able to use the Safety Car to his advantage and secured P6 at the chequered flag

"It feels good to have such a good turnaround. I have to say a massive thanks to the team for making it possible for me to get back into the weekend after the crash on Friday, I think it was a really big one. So I owe it to them for the points I scored this weekend."

The ART driver also reflected on how difficult the weekend was without accumulating the mileage of his rivals.

After his crash left him out of Practice and on the sidelines for Qualifying, he was very happy with the speed he and the team were able to show having taken lessons from Saturday's Sprint Race.

READ MORE

Gabriele Minì: 'Title not out of reach' after aggressive drive to points in Madrid

Hiyu Yamakoshi to race with Van Amersfoort Racing in Baku

He added that it boded well for the remainder of the season, with his points on Sunday adding to his Feature Race scoring streak that goes back to Round 6.

"It is very satisfying. Track time was very crucial with it being a new track for everyone and not an easy one as well.

"So everything was about track time on Friday and unfortunately we had none. So yesterday in the Sprint Race, it was about collecting the mileage and learning the track as much as possible and getting prepared as much as possible for today.

Inthraphuvasak is optimistic that he and ART can carry their momentum on into Baku

"I think the pace was really, really good today and it was a positive after what happened on Friday."

Up next will be Baku, another new track for Inthraphuvasak and many on the 2026 grid. The very fast street circuit will put drivers to the test once more, but after his Madrid comeback, Inthraphuvasak says he's carrying confidence into Round 12.

"I really can't wait to get back in the car. I think this weekend prepares all the drivers, not just myself, very well for Baku.

"It's a street circuit again, but one that I have never been to. So, same process as this weekend, learn as much as possible on the sim and try to start on a very good level FP.

"It's been a few good rounds, a bit of a setback this weekend, but I'm sure that I'm going to be back on top of it very soon."

Next Up

title: Gabriele Minì: 'Title not out of reach' after aggressive drive to points in Madrid
excerpt:
MP Motorsport's Gabriele Minì was able to mount a spirited fightback in Madrid after a tough Qualifying session left him starting down the order.

The Italian recovered from 13th on the Feature Race grid to wind up inside the points with seventh place marking a solid recovery drive.

Looking back at his race, Minì talked through his approach, as he picked off several rivals at Turn 13 making overtakes that he says were 'big sends' out of La Monumental.

"Started P13, I got a very good start, but because of that I got sandwiched between two cars, so I had to slow down, and I think I actually lost position there, it was just a mess at the beginning.

"I tried surviving, and I gained three positions, so three nice overtakes, and to be honest we just managed up until the Safety Car

"I managed to overtake Ollie and then I extended the stint. We then decided to pit because we felt like it was a good moment to get the two cars ahead. But sadly a Safety Car just came after that.

"That was a big shame, we lost four places because if the timing of the Safety Car had been lucky for us, we could have been in P4. Instead, we restarted P8. So then again, I had to do a big send for P7, but then the three cars ahead were on fresh option tyres, and we know it's a big difference around here.

"We just had to try and see if they were going to make a mistake, which happened at some point, but there was no space to make a pass."

The Italian is still in the title race currently third in the standings with 153 points

With overtaking proving difficult around the Madring, the Alpine Academy talent says that his moves were more instinctive than planned.

His progress stood out with other drivers opting for a more conservative approach, but his current Championship position means that aggressive moves were required.

"To be honest, the moves weren't really planned. I was like, OK, more or less we can do it. So I just sent it and then we'll see what happens after. It worked most of the time. Sometimes it didn't because I sent it too hard, but I was never really in an overtaking spot.

READ MORE

Alexander Dunne: 'I'll leave nothing on the table' in pursuit of title

Hiyu Yamakoshi to race with Van Amersfoort Racing in Baku

"That's why nobody really defended. I think I was braking 15 metres later than what I usually do. And it was working, to be honest. It was good, but we're getting to the end of the Championship and I knew I needed to make moves up the order.

"Either you do this or you go home with regrets. That's not what I want to do. I prefer to crash into a wall trying than not trying at all."

Minì remains third in the Drivers' Standings but was able to take several points out of leader Nikola Tsolov.

The MP driver says Qualifying form will need to improve in Baku in order to fight for the top positions

Heading to Baku, the MP driver now sits 24 points adrift in the Drivers' Championship, well within range considering there will be an additional Qualifying and Feature Race in Azerbaijan next time out.

The Italian says that he feels the gap isn't too big to overturn in the final rounds of the 2026 campaign, but that there will need to be a step made in one-lap speed in particular in order to challenge for the title.

"I think we can still be happy. We gained six points to the leader this weekend and considering two contenders started the Feature in P3 and in P5, leaving here gaining points is not bad.

"We see Alex is getting close as well. We just need to sort out our quali. I think in Baku everything is still open.

"We know in motorsport that anything can happen. We know we can do it, we just have to go with the mentality of not having much to lose and trying to maximise everything, as always.

"We have a bit to figure out, we know what's going on, but we have to figure qualifying out in particular. Starting at the front, I think we can fight for better positions."

title: Hiyu Yamakoshi to race with Van Amersfoort Racing in Baku
excerpt:
Van Amersfoort Racing has confirmed that Hiyu Yamakoshi will step up to FIA Formula 2 and drive for the team in Baku in place of Nico Varrone.

The Japanese driver competed in FIA Formula 3 this season with the Dutch outfit, securing a top 10 finish in the Drivers’ Championship, with three podiums and a pole position en route to ninth in the Standings.

Yamakoshi will now be gearing up to take on the Baku City Circuit in just over a weeks’ time, a prospect he says he is very much looking forward to.

“I’m very happy to have this opportunity to make my Formula 2 debut with VAR. I’ve been with the team since F4, so stepping into F2 together makes this a very special moment. I’m looking forward to learning as much as possible throughout the weekend, working with the team and making the most of the experience.”

Van Amersfoort Team Principal Brad Joyce added: “We’re pleased to give Hiyu the opportunity to make his Formula 2 debut in Baku. He has made strong progress this season and has shown his pace in F3, with several strong results throughout his rookie campaign. Having worked with Hiyu for three years, we know his approach and his ability to learn. This will be a new challenge for him, and we’re looking forward to working with him throughout the weekend.

“At the same time, we would like to thank Nico for his work with the team this season. He has been a valued member of our F2 line-up, and we have really enjoyed having him as part of the team. Coming from sports car racing, the move to Formula 2 was a significant change, and Nico adapted very well to the demands of single-seater racing. He took on that challenge and showed that he could adapt to Formula 2 in a very short period of time. We wish him all the best for the next steps in his career.”

title: Alexander Dunne: 'I'll leave nothing on the table' in pursuit of title
excerpt:
It was P2 in the Madrid Feature Race for Alexander Dunne on a good weekend for the Rodin driver

It was a positive weekend in Madrid for Alexander Dunne. The Rodin Motorsport driver made a return to the podium for the first time since Barcelona's Feature Race.

Though the Irishman has achieved four top five finishes and a further four top 10 finishes in that time, it was a good result according to Dunne, as he was pleased with single-lap and race pace all weekend.

"I feel good, I'm very happy," Dunne reflected. "I'm not normally this happy to finish second, so I'll take it while it lasts. I think it was a good weekend. Qualifying was strong, race pace was very strong. I think ultimately Dino did a very good job this weekend, his pace was very strong.

"I think he and I were probably quite a bit quicker than the rest of the grid, so I think in general the pace and that sort of thing was really strong.

"I'm very pleased, I think the team and I made a good step. One that I really hope we can continue to carry forward for the rest of the year. Overall, I think it was a very good weekend."

Dunne was back on the F2 podium and says the team's performance was much more in line with expectations

The Madrid Feature Race was a tricky race strategically, with an early Safety Car leaving many teams and driver split on when to make their mandatory stop.

While Dunne was initially wanting to come in at the first opportunity, so much so he had openly told his team over the radio that was his preference, the Rodin driver ran longer in the end.

It proved to be the correct choice, with another Safety Car providing him and eventual race winner Dino Beganovic the ideal opportunity to pit and emerge without losing track position.

READ MORE

FIA Formula 2 announce supersized Baku Round

Dunne explained the thinking behind those early laps and how the strategy calls evolved in a race that continued to ebb and flow in and out of favour of the title contenders.

"It was really difficult. Ultimately, if there's a Safety Car on Lap 6, you can come in for a free pit stop, but then you also have the possibility of getting stuck behind someone who's slower than you. I think you need to have a massive pace advantage to be able to get past them again.

"Realistically, we made the right decision. I managed the Soft tyre as well, I was able to extend quite long and we got the chance to wait for that second Safety Car.

The Irish driver is still aiming for the F2 title and took a big chunk of points out of leader Tsolov

"If you look at Rafa and Martinius, who were behind me, they had to pit a little bit early to cover off someone who had pitted before them.

"In the end, that kind of destroyed their race. I was considering pitting not too long after they did, but I'm very glad I didn't."

With Baku up next, Dunne's weekend in Madrid closed the gap down to Championship leader Nikola Tsolov. There is still plenty of ground to make up, with 38 points separating the Irish driver in P4 and the points leader.

Round 12 will be a supersized round, with an extra Qualifying and Feature Race providing even more points, and Dunne says he'll be aiming to maximise his chances of catching the Bulgarian.

"I'm pushing hard to try and get at least in the top three. I think it's going to be difficult, but we've been improving at the moment. For sure, as a driver, I'm going to leave nothing on the table, leave it all out there. I think we should end up in a good place."

Next Up

title: Freddie Slater signs with Invicta Racing for 2027 F2 campaign
excerpt:
Freddie Slater will graduate up to FIA Formula 2 next season with Invicta Racing. The team is the first to announce a driver for the 2027 campaign, with the 2026 FIA Formula 3 runner-up joining the current F2 Teams’ Champions.

Slater secured one race victory this season in F3 along with a further seven podium finishes and three pole positions en route to P2 in the Drivers’ Standings.

Prior to F3, the Audi Driver Development Programme talent earned titles in the Formula Regional European Championship in 2025, Italian and UAE F4 titles in 2024 and the Ginetta Junior Championship in 2023.

Slater said that he was eager to begin work with his new team ahead of the 2027 campaign. “I’m really excited to be stepping up to Formula 2 with Invicta Racing next year. I learned a lot in Formula 3 this season, and I feel I have developed as a driver and as a person over the course of the year. Invicta has a great record in Formula 2, and I cannot wait to get started with the team and prepare for our campaign together. I am also very grateful for the continued support from the Audi Driver Development Programme. There is still a lot for me to learn, and I’m really looking forward to taking on this new challenge.”

Invicta Racing CEO and Team Principal James Robinson added: “We’re delighted to welcome Freddie to Invicta Racing for 2027. To finish runner-up in the FIA Formula 3 Championship in his first season is an outstanding achievement, particularly given the level of competition in the category. His results throughout the year, including a victory, three pole positions and eight podiums, underline the pace and consistency he has shown. Freddie has demonstrated that he is ready for the next challenge, and we’re very excited to help him take that next step in Formula 2.”

Allan McNish, Director, Audi Driver Development Programme said: “The move to Formula 2 is the natural next step for Freddie, and an important new phase of his development as a driver. He enjoyed a strong Formula 3 season, fighting for the title until the final round - showing his speed, racecraft and progress throughout the year. We are very proud of what Freddie has achieved this season and how he has developed along the way. Invicta Racing has had an excellent record in recent years, and we are delighted to be working with them. We believe it is the ideal environment for him, and we look forward to supporting him as he takes on this new challenge in 2027.”

title: FIA Formula 2 announce supersized Baku Round
excerpt:
The FIA Formula 2 Championship announce that Round 12 of the F2 2026 season, which will take place on 24-26 September at the Baku City Circuit, will be enhanced, with an additional Qualifying session and a second Feature Race.

The final two rounds of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will resume with the usual weekend format made of one Free Practice followed by one Qualifying, a Sprint Race and a Feature Race.

Bruno Michel, FIA Formula 2 CEO said: “As Formula 2 is the only Support Event at the Azerbaijan Formula 1 Grand Prix, together with the promoters, we have opted for a supersized F2 race weekend, with one Free Practice, two Qualifying sessions, one Sprint Race and two Feature Races.

“This is the only weekend where the Timetable allows the additional sessions, which will increase the level of entertainment even further for the attending crowd and all our fans. The Baku City Circuit always provides us with amazing racing, so we’re very pleased to make the 12th Round of our season pretty unique.

“We will then revert to our usual race weekend format for the final two rounds of the 2026 season, which will be held at Doha and Yas Marina.”

Round 12 schedule will consist of:

Thursday morning: one 45-minute Free Practice session.

Thursday afternoon: two consecutive 20-minute Qualifying sessions.

Friday morning: Sprint Race, with the reverse-grid order determined by the results of the first Qualifying session.

Friday afternoon: First Feature Race, with the starting grid set by the results of the first Qualifying session.

Saturday morning: Second Feature Race, with the grid determined by the results of the second Qualifying session. Pole position in each Qualifying session will award 2 points, while both Feature Races will carry the standard points allocation, including 1 point for Fastest Lap, providing they are in the top 10 positions of the final race classification, in accordance with the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.

title: Round 11 Post-Feature Race Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2: Welcome, everyone, to today’s FIA Formula 2 Press Conference following the Feature Race here in Madrid. Joining us is Ritomo Miyata of Hitech in third, Alexander Dunne of Rodin Motorsport in second, and Dino Beganovic of DAMS Lucas Oil, who has claimed his first Feature Race victory in Formula 2. Congratulations, Dino. A dominant victory and your first Feature Race win. How does that feel?

Dino Beganovic: It obviously feels very good. It has been a while and I feel like we have been waiting for this one for a long time. It feels very good to get it here after a very good Friday.

FIA Formula 2: You looked completely dialled in. Tell us about the car the team gave you this weekend.

Beganovic: Honestly, the team did a good job all week. We came from the simulator having tested some things and went in a direction they had not been used to before, but it obviously worked this weekend. Hopefully, we can carry it on to Baku. From Free Practice, I felt very good and confident in the car, and that is all you need at this track.

FIA Formula 2: You started on the soft tyre. How did it hold up during your first stint?

Beganovic: Honestly, the soft tyre was very good today and yesterday. It was very fast and the grip was solid. At the start of the race, we were quite slow and tried to remain flexible with what we could do. Once the first few drivers pitted, we knew what to do. We picked up our pace and were able to match them and then go quicker, which was a good sign. Everything went to plan and the Safety Car was a bonus for us.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations on the victory. Alex, congratulations on P2. Can you take us through your race?

Alexander Dunne: I think it was a good one and I am very happy. The Soft tyre had quite a lot of performance, more than I expected, even with how strong it looked in the Sprint Race yesterday. Most of the drivers who used it yesterday gained places and maintained them, whereas I expected the tyre to degrade a little more towards the end. The performance of the soft tyre, our first tyre today, helped Dino and me finish where we did. We were able to extend the first stint for a long time and wait for a Safety Car. Even without one, if you had asked me to do another 10 laps at the same level of performance, I think I could have done it. I was impressed by how good the soft tyres felt. They degraded to a certain point and then did not get any worse. The lap times stayed consistent. That was the key to having a good race today.

FIA Formula 2: Were you able to use the Hard tyre and push a little more towards the end of the race?

Dunne: Definitely a little. For whatever reason, it was much more physical on the hard tyre. Physicality and steering weight were things we discussed coming into the weekend, and particularly today because the race was 10 laps longer than yesterday. On the soft tyre, it was not too difficult, but on the hard tyre it was really tough. The steering weight through Turn 12 and all the high-speed corners was very demanding. At the end, I had to back off because, if I had pushed slightly over the limit, I do not think I would have been able to catch the car because the steering was so heavy. We need to understand why it felt so different between the soft and hard tyres. The pace was still very strong and we managed to set the fastest lap as well, which was good.

FIA Formula 2: Describe the physicality of the race. Through La Monumental, it looked as though you were pulling some very high G-forces.

Dunne: It was crazy. I saw a video the other day saying that the corner is more than 500 metres long. We go through there at over 200 kilometres per hour and there is a lot of banking, which naturally puts much more load through the car. It is also where we have the most downforce, so the steering becomes really heavy. It was pretty tough. At the end, I had to back off a little through Turn 12 because it was too difficult and not worth risking an incident. Up to that point, I think we got the most out of it.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations on P2, Alex. Ritomo, congratulations. Hitech appeared to give you a very good car this weekend. How did it feel?

Ritomo Miyata: It is amazing to be back on the podium. We finished P3 after starting P9. The strategy was good and the Safety Car helped us gain positions, but we also had good pace. That is why we are here.

FIA Formula 2: How physically challenging was it for you today?

Miyata: Turn 12 and the banking were definitely very tough. The steering feedback was heavy. I came from Super Formula, where they have power steering, so Formula 2 has much heavier steering and is physically demanding. Today was very different compared with yesterday. The prime stint was very tough physically.

FIA Formula 2: How was the tyre degradation over the race distance?

Miyata: The tyre degradation was quite flat and not too high, but Turn 12 became much more physically demanding. It was difficult to drive on the limit because, if you pushed too much, the car could slide and feel unpredictable, and it was difficult to add steering input because it was so heavy. I tried to stay just under the limit there and then push in Sectors 1 and 3.

title: Round 11 Post-Sprint Race Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2: Welcome everyone to today's FIA Formula 2 Press Conference following the Sprint Race in Madrid. Joining us are P3 from Trident, Laurens van Hoepen, P2 from AIX Racing, Emerson Fittipaldi, and from Hitech, claiming his first Formula 2 victory, Ritomo Miyata. Ritomo, congratulations on the victory. How does that one feel?

Ritomo Miyata: I am really happy. Finally we won a race because we have struggled during the season. To finally win is a really good feeling.

FIA Formula 2: Take me through the start because you had a great one.

Miyata: I was expecting an overtake opportunity at the start, so I really focused on the launch. We managed the race well from there.

FIA Formula 2: It is the first win for Hitech since Baku last year. Tell me about the car they gave you today.

Miyata: This year I expected much more, but during the season we struggled, especially on short-run performance. We analysed everything during the summer break and finally came back with strong performance. That is why we won today, and since Monza we have been back to our level.

FIA Formula 2: Emerson, congratulations on P2 and your first Formula 2 podium. How does that feel?

Emerson Fittipaldi: It feels great to be on the podium in Formula 2 in my rookie season. Doing it with AIX is incredible. We have worked hard all season through a lot of challenges and difficulties. It is always rewarding to stand on the podium after all that effort.

FIA Formula 2: Laurens was chasing you at the end. How hard was it to hold him off?

Fittipaldi: It was quite tough. The car was not easy to drive and I was struggling quite a lot, but I kept it on the track and managed to finish P2.

FIA Formula 2: You started on the Hard tyre. How was the degradation?

Fittipaldi: This track is very demanding on the tyres because it has high-speed, medium-speed and low-speed corners. It is a tough circuit and I think tomorrow will be a great race as well.

FIA Formula 2: Laurens, congratulations on P3. Can you take me through your move on Noel?

Laurens van Hoepen: The start was not great, but after that we had good pace, partly because of the compound we were on. I knew I had to make the move at some point. Overtaking is very difficult here, so I prepared it as much as possible and when I saw my chance I went for it. It worked out well and it was a calculated move.

FIA Formula 2: Talk us through the closing laps when you were behind Emerson.

Van Hoepen: It is hard to follow on this track because overtaking opportunities are limited. I was trying to pressure him into a mistake, but my tyres were fading as well. I got close a few times but it was not enough.

FIA Formula 2: You started on the Soft tyre. Did you know it would remain competitive for the whole race?

Van Hoepen: That was the plan. We hoped it would be a little stronger at the start and maybe weaker at the end, but the performance stayed quite similar throughout the race. That was positive, although it is a shame we could not make more of it.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations on P3.

Thirdly, Sebastiàn Montoya has been given permission to start both races in Madrid.

Finally, Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak has been given permission to start both races in Madrid.

Inthraphuvasak is set to start from P22 on the Sprint Race grid.

title: Fittipaldi ready to capitalise on best F2 Qualifying result in Madrid
excerpt:
Emerson Fittipaldi secured P10 in the FIA Formula 2 Qualifying session in Madrid, a season-best result for the AIX Racing driver.

The Brazilian left it late in the day but kept his cool under pressure having had an earlier laptime deleted for exceeding track limits.

Reflecting on his session back in the paddock, Fittipaldi explained just how difficult the session was to manage from the cockpit.

"I'm very, very happy. I can only thank God for this result. It was a very stressful and chaotic qualifying as everybody saw.

"It's a very technical and difficult track and finally we got the car in the window where we could be competitive and in the top 10 and that's amazing.

"Because no one's been here before, I think that really helped level things out. Most of the other races this season, it was my first time there when all the others had already raced there, so that has been a big disadvantage.

"Today was very fair and the team managed to give me a very nice car and finally we have a top 10 and reverse pole tomorrow, so it's an amazing weekend already."

Diving deeper into his session, Fittipaldi explained how his qualifying session took shape, with the AIX driver losing an earlier effort to a track limits violation.

Along with that, the three Red Flag stoppages meant that there was no time to get into a rhythm during the half-hour session, and that it all came down to that final lap.

"Up until the last push of the whole qualifying session, I didn't have a lap in," Fittipaldi explained. "I was dead last, so it was very, very stressful. I got track limits and red flags here and there and you're like, 'oh my God, what am I going to do now?'

"Then in the last lap, I was like, let me give it everything I have and that was enough to put me in top 10, so that was good."

Looking ahead to the remainder of the Madrid weekend, Fittipaldi is aiming to capitalise on his strong grid position for both races.

Overtaking is set to be tricky according to the drivers, meaning that reverse grid pole potentially holds even more value around the Madring.

The AIX driver isn't getting carried away however, and is focused on executing a clean weekend from here on out.

"Hoping for the best result possible. I don't want to add any extra pressure, just enjoy starting from the front row and do the best I can.

"I know that the team will give me the best car that they can do because the engineers have been working so hard this year and we've been working so much to try to develop and improve to be closer to the top teams. Finally, now we're getting there.

"I think it's going to happen mostly off the line, that's where most people are going to get their overtakes done. I'm in a pretty good position, I think, for tomorrow's race because it's a track where you really cannot overtake easily and it's very challenging.

"I'll just do the best race I can tomorrow and see where we finish."
